summary: A landscaped lawn with trees on Mission Bay South's plan Block 22; not a formally named park in any source checked. Pier & Point's own satellite review found no building footprint on the site, and a September 2026 on-site visit by Pier & Point confirmed it is already a completed small park rather than still-planned open space, correcting an earlier satellite-only assessment. No independently published source (a city agency, news outlet or landscape-architecture record) naming or dating it was found.

open_questions: No independently published source (SF Recreation & Park Department, OCII, news coverage) names or dates this park; the only evidence found is Pier & Point's own satellite-imagery review and its September 2026 on-site confirmation that it is already built, both recorded in the mapping log for this record's shape -- not a substitute for a dated public-record source, so no completion milestone is asserted here.

Pier & Point's earlier DataSF Assessor Parcels/Building Footprints check (recorded in the same mapping log) traced the dominant underlying parcel to a retired 1998 'COMMON_AREAS' placeholder (blklot 8799TBA3, dropped 2005) plus scattered UCSF campus parcel fragments -- consistent with open, non-built land, but that doesn't establish when the current landscaping was actually built.
Not clear whether this block corresponds to any of OCII's lettered/numbered open-space plan parcels (P1-P27) tracked elsewhere in this project; no such label was found for it in any source checked.

Possible identity, not confirmed: UCSF's June 12, 2025 CAC presentation (p.3 map, 'MAP UPDATED: DECEMBER 2024', read directly 2026-09-29) labels a park 'KORET QUAD (22)' in the North Campus, and OCII's Nov 14, 2024 'Mission Bay Future Parks' CAC update (p.2 map) is reported to label a completed park 'Koret Quad' in this block's position, and Wikipedia's Mission Bay article lists Koret Quad among parks complete by fall 2010. Whether this block is Koret Quad still needs to be confirmed before the record is renamed or its 'complete' status is sourced to that map; until then the status rests only on Pier & Point's September 2026 site visit.
